Exhaustive search over stepped-wedge and wait-list allocations

Source: R/stepped_wedge.R
sw_design_search.Rd

Enumerates every integer allocation of G clusters to start periods 2, ..., T and a wait-list (at least one cluster starting in period 2), subject to a rollout cap and a maximum wait-list size, and evaluates the ETI cost, IT variance ratio and adequacy radius of each (equal cluster-period sizes). The optimum is over this finite set only.

Usage

sw_design_search(
  G,
  T,
  cap = Inf,
  max_wait = G - 1,
  phi = NULL,
  icc = NULL,
  cac = 1,
  m = NULL,
  estimator = c("GLS", "TWFE"),
  objective = c("eti_cost", "radius"),
  max_it_ratio = Inf,
  top = 1,
  alpha = 0.05,
  epsilon = 0.05,
  power = 0.8
)

Arguments

G

number of clusters

T

number of periods

cap

maximum number of clusters starting in any one period

max_wait

maximum number of wait-listed clusters

phi

Hussey–Hughes parameter \(\phi = m\rho/(1-\rho)\) (GLS); Inf gives the fixed-effects limit.

icc, cac, m

alternative nested-exchangeable specification: within-period ICC, cluster autocorrelation and individuals per cluster-period (see [sw_phi_nested()]). With sizes, m is not needed.

estimator

"GLS" (default) or "TWFE" (two-way fixed effects, which does not use the covariance).

objective

"eti_cost" (minimise the ETI cost) or "radius" (maximise \(\kappa^*\) subject to it_ratio <= max_it_ratio)

max_it_ratio

IT-variance constraint for objective = "radius"

top

number of best designs returned

alpha, epsilon, power

radius calibration (see [sw_radius()])

Value

list with best (data frame of the top designs), frontier (best objective for each wait-list size bound 0, ..., max_wait) and designs (all evaluated designs)

Examples

# \donttest{
s <- sw_design_search(G = 24, T = 5, cap = 6, max_wait = 12, phi = 2)
s$frontier[s$frontier$max_wait %in% c(0, 4, 6, 8, 12), ]
#>    max_wait start2 start3 start4 start5 wait eti_cost  it_ratio    radius
#> 1         0      6      6      6      6    0 2.269942 1.0000000 0.1332467
#> 5         4      6      6      2      6    4 1.519707 0.9237537 0.1819003
#> 7         6      6      6      0      6    6 1.376921 0.9459459 0.2129412
#> 9         8      6      6      1      3    8 1.290928 0.9563567 0.2491485
#> 13       12      6      6      1      0   11 1.227424 1.0508757 0.3768735
# }
